events.summary:
At 1032 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain continue across the warned area this morning, where
between 2.5 and 4.5 inches of rain have already fallen overnight and
this morning. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Olean, Salamanca, Allegany State Park, Allegany, St. Bonaventure,
Weston Mills, Hinsdale, Carrollton, Portville, Vandalia, Knapp
Creek, Rock City Park, Limestone, Kill Buck, Haskell Flats, Ceres,
Little Genesee and Allegheny Reservoir.

events.region: Northern Baltimore; Cecil; Southern Baltimore; Anne Arundel; Central and Southeast Howard; Northwest Harford; Southeast Harford
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of central, northeast, and northern Maryland,
including the following areas, in central Maryland, Anne Arundel
and Central and Southeast Howard. In northeast Maryland, Cecil. In
northern Maryland, Northern Baltimore, Northwest Harford,
Southeast Harford and Southern Baltimore.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Strong to severe thunderstorms are likely to push across the
area this afternoon and evening with a humid air mass in
place. Very heavy rainfall rates are possible in these
storms. These rates could approach 1 to 2 inches per hour,
with higher instantaneous rates possible. The most vulnerable
locations would be urbanized areas along I-95 as well as
areas which have experienced heavy rainfall in recent days.
- Please visit www.weather.gov/safety/flood for flood safety
and preparedness information.

events.region: Wet Mountains between 6300 and 10000Ft; Wet Mountains above 10000 Ft; Pueblo Vicinity/Pueblo County Below 6300 Feet
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows caused by excessive rainfall
continue to be possible over the Aspen Acres burn scar.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Colorado, including the following
areas, Pueblo County in the vicinity of the Aspen Acres burn scar,
and the Wet Mountains Above 6300 Feet.

* WHEN...From noon MDT today through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Heavy rainfall over the Aspen Acres burn scar is expected
up to and during the period of the watch. Residents near the Aspen
Acres burn scar should prepare for potential debris flow. Be sure
to stay up to date with information from local authorities. Heavy
rainfall could trigger flash flooding of low-lying areas, urbanized
street flooding, and debris flows in and near recent wildfire burn
scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- National Weather Service Meteorologists are forecasting the
potential for heavy rainfall over the burn scar, which may lead
to flash flooding and debris flows.
- Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Beulah, San Isabel, Greenhorn Mountain, Rye, Colorado City and
Rosita.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
AQAMT

The Montana Department of Environmental Quality has issued an air
quality alert for Beaverhead, Blaine, Broadwater, Cascade, Chouteau,
Deer Lodge, Fergus, Granite, Jefferson, Judith Basin, Lake, Lewis and
Clark, Liberty, Meagher, Mineral, Missoula, Petroleum, Pondera,
Powell, Ravalli, Sanders, Silver Bow, Teton, Toole, Phillips, Hill
counties in effect until 9AM on 07/29/2026
An Air Quality Alert means that particulates have been trending
upwards and that an exceedance of the 24 hour National Ambient Air
Quality Standard (NAAQS) has occurred or may occur in the near
future.

Elevated particulate levels from wildfire smoke

As of 6AM on 07/28/2026, particulate levels in Billings, Hamilton and
Helena are Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups.

As of 6AM on 07/28/2026, particulate levels in Butte, Columbia Falls,
Cut Bank, Dillon, Frenchtown, Great Falls, Havre, Lewistown, Libby,
Malta, Missoula, Sleeping Giant and Thompson Falls are Moderate.

When air quality is Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups... State and local
health officials recommend that people with respiratory or heart
disease, the elderly and children should limit prolonged exertion.

When air quality is Moderate... State and local health officials
recommend that unusually sensitive people should consider reducing
prolonged or heavy exertion.

For more information visit the Montana Department of Environmental
Quality at http://todaysair.mtdeq.us
